text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE STRAITS TIMES:

- Since claiming victory in the July 5-6 fighting against forces of factional rivals, troops loyal to Cambodian strongman Hun Sen round up hundreds of opponents and execute many, while frightened politicians and journalists remain in hiding or scramble for seats on few planes out of capital.
- Two Australians die and at least 40 others are injured when bridge collapses at opening of international Jewish sporting event in Israel, officials say.
- Japan calls on Cambodian royalist party of Prince Norodom Ranariddh to choose new co-premier, voicing hopes Second Prime Minister Hun Sen would then form new coalition.
- Mardan Mamat becomes first Singapore golfer to qualify for British Open, which tees off on Thursday.

- World-renowned fashion designer Gianni Versace, 50, shot and killed outside his mansion on Miami Beach, hospital source says. Shooting takes place after he walked back from having breakfast at cafe a few blocks away.

- QAF rises from baker of Gardenia loaves to one of South-east Asia's largest food groups with its Singapore $2.75 billion purchase of majority stake in parent Salim group's PT Indo-food Sukses Makmur.
- Complex QAF deal will give clove cigarette tycoon Putera Sampoerna a second foothold in Singapore stock exchange after takeover of mainboard-listed Transmarco last year.
- Ayala Corp, Philippines' oldest conglomerate, plans to acquire at least 20 percent in consortium gearing up to buy Forum The Shopping Mall in Orchard Road, sources say.
- Malaysia Acting Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim lashes out at currency speculators, but also concedes there are limits to what governments can do to fend off such concerted actions.
THE BUSINESS TIMES:

- Acting Malaysia Prime Minister Anwar confirms major dispute has arisen with main contractor of M$15.5 billion Bakun dam in Sarawak, and is expected to delay both construction and public listing of national project.
- Indonesia's controversial national car project, PT Timor Putra Nasional, thrown into jeopardy by news its Korean partner, Kia Motors, has come under bankruptcy protection.
- Selling pressure eases somewhat but Southeast Asian currencies remain weak, as do equity markets with exception of Hongkong. Ringgit again attracts market's attention after Anwar's remarks.
- Parkway Holdings may spin off primary healthcare business into separate listed entity -- which, if successful, would make it second such play here after Raffles Medical Group.
- Property group DBS Land appoints Bertie Cheng Shao Shiong, Foo Kok Swee and Winston Choo Wee Leong to board of directors.

- Creative Technology share price recovery in last few months catapults two of its founders into upper echelons of Singapore's millionaire league and lifts chairman Sim Wong Hoo's portfolio to three-quarters of a billion Singapore dollars.
- Creative Technology shares hit S$30 level before closing at three-year high of S$29.80 on expectations of solid year-end results.
- CAM International Holdings says has completed sale of 49 percent stake in aeroponics venture to Sime Darby subsidiary Consolidated Plantations Berhad for S$10.88 million.
- Singapore Airlines foreign shares were lower amid continuing concern about regional currencies and possible uncertainty about the company's future treatment of its foreign shares, analysts say.
